scope.method: Read all six full DE/EN expectation, variation and two-case bodies against current canonical goal wording and earlier independently checked direct source and image contexts. Verified each current active image SHA against its AI visualization-QA record. The excluded 92c image-changing goal was not reviewed as a P profile.
scope.limits: Technical profile validity is separate from scientific/scope judgment. This review does not register P in the central five-gate registry, approve D/A/M/V or claim human release approval.

targetedCheck.result: Technical PASS: configured 6, blocking issues 0, needs human review 6, approved 0. The two content HOLDs below remain additional blockers.

decisions.finding: Both supplied-data cases correctly distinguish mobile electrons in copper, mobile ions in aqueous NaCl and molten KBr, fixed ions in solid salts, and neutral molecules in sugar solution/pure ethanol. The new melt case transfers beyond the existing picture and explicitly avoids practical heating. Observation and particle model are separated; DE/EN and current page/image agree.

The supplied Li and Mg successive ionization energies are plausible rounded values and their large jumps occur after removing respectively one and two outer electrons, consistent with simple 2,1 and 2,8,2 shell allocations. Neither case treats the measured energies as proof of literal circular orbits or orbital shape. DE/EN and current sodium image context agree.

The neutral P and Ca atomic numbers, valence counts and periods are correct, and the image is current. However the canonical competence asks for periodic-table deductions about atoms. This profile makes ion-charge electron accounting an essential/observable requirement and requires P3− and Ca2+ calculations in both independent demonstrations. Those may be useful optional boundary contrasts, but as required mastery evidence they extend beyond this goal's authored atom scope. A technical PASS does not validate that scope expansion.
decisions.requiredResolution: Keep the two required independent demonstrations within neutral main-group atom/PSE reasoning, or substantively revise and re-review the canonical goal/source scope if ion competence is intended. Ion contrasts can remain optional and must not become a hidden mastery prerequisite.

decisions.finding: Copper and aluminium cases ask learners to derive a simple metal model from conductivity plus malleability, explain why rigid isolated Dalton spheres fail, and use conductive brittle graphite as a counterexample to overgeneralization. The model is stated as qualitative, not a band-structure claim. This matches the current canonical goal and direct BY property-to-model source.

H2O versus NaCl and independent CO2 versus CaF2 cases correctly contrast a discrete covalent molecule with an extended ionic lattice. Ca2+ and two F− give 1:2 charge-neutral formula units without inventing CaF2 molecules. Identical 1:2 digits across CO2/CaF2 force particle-structure reasoning beyond memorized formula pattern.

The H2O/CO2 and NH3/CH4 VSEPR cases otherwise count domains, lone pairs and shapes correctly. The second expected-performance sentence says NH3 is not a `sichtbaren Tetraeder aus vier Atomen` / `visible four-atom tetrahedron`. NH3 has four atoms, and its N plus three H nuclei are noncoplanar; the wording conflates a missing fourth bonded partner with the count of visible atoms. It can misteach the intended distinction between tetrahedral electron-domain geometry and trigonal-pyramidal molecular geometry.
decisions.requiredResolution: State instead that the N lone pair is not a fourth bonded atom and NH3 remains trigonal-pyramidal; preserve the correct four-domain count and CH4 comparison, then rematerialize and recheck the affected profile.
